## Dataset and business question

```{=html}

     smaller reduces slide text size. self-contained bundles the HTML resources.
     R analysis follows the PCA tutorial and descriptive-analysis notes. -->
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse, tidymodels, here, gt)
tidymodels_prefer()

# Ahmad Sufi confirmed as leader. Last five student-ID digits confirmed in chat.
set.seed(41352)

phones <- here("data/smartphone_cleaned_v5.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE)
glimpse(phones)

# Match Person B's existing preparation so Person A can render independently.
# At the final group merge, run this preparation only once.
# Only unavailable fast charging is recoded to zero. Unknown values stay NA.
phones_recoded <- phones |>
  mutate(
    fast_charging = if_else(fast_charging_available == 0, 0, fast_charging),
    log_price = log(price),
    brand_group = fct_lump_n(brand_name, n = 5),
    has_5g = factor(has_5g),
    has_nfc = factor(has_nfc)
  )

phones_clean <- phones_recoded |>
  select(
    log_price, processor_speed, ram_capacity, internal_memory,
    refresh_rate, fast_charging, primary_camera_rear,
    primary_camera_front, rating, battery_capacity,
    has_5g, has_nfc, brand_group
  ) |>
  na.omit()

# Keep the tutorial's split. Scenario 6 does not require prediction assessment.
phone_split <- initial_split(phones_clean, prop = 0.75)
phone_training <- training(phone_split)
phone_test <- testing(phone_split)

phone_recipe <- recipe(log_price ~ ., data = phone_training) |>
  step_normalize(
    processor_speed, ram_capacity, internal_memory, refresh_rate,
    fast_charging, primary_camera_rear, primary_camera_front
  ) |>
  step_pca(
    processor_speed, ram_capacity, internal_memory, refresh_rate,
    fast_charging, primary_camera_rear, primary_camera_front,
    threshold = 0.7, id = "pca"
  ) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors())

phone_prep <- prep(phone_recipe)

# bake() removes the original factor columns after dummy coding.
# Attach labels from exactly the same rows, in exactly the same order.
pc_scores <- phone_training |>
  select(has_5g, brand_group) |>
  bind_cols(
    bake(phone_prep, new_data = phone_training) |>
      select(starts_with("PC"))
  )
pc_names <- names(pc_scores |> select(starts_with("PC")))
num_pcs <- length(pc_names)
var_tbl <- tidy(phone_prep, id = "pca", type = "variance")
loading_tbl <- tidy(phone_prep, id = "pca", type = "coef")
retained_variance <- var_tbl |>
  filter(terms == "cumulative percent variance", component == num_pcs) |>
  pull(value)

pca_vars <- phones_clean |>
  select(
    processor_speed, ram_capacity, internal_memory, refresh_rate,
    fast_charging, primary_camera_rear, primary_camera_front
  )
correlation_matrix <- cor(pca_vars)

pc_by_5g <- pc_scores |>
  group_by(has_5g) |>
  summarise(n = n(), across(starts_with("PC"), mean), .groups = "drop")
pc_by_brand <- pc_scores |>
  group_by(brand_group) |>
  summarise(n = n(), across(starts_with("PC"), mean), .groups = "drop")

# Descriptive summaries refer to the 784 complete records, before splitting.
numeric_summary <- phones_clean |>
  summarise(across(
    where(is.numeric),
    list(mean = mean, sd = sd, median = median, min = min, max = max),
    .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", ".value"), names_sep = "__")

# Include categorical and helper variables used in cleaning, even with zero NAs.
missing_vars <- c(
  "price", "processor_speed", "ram_capacity", "internal_memory",
  "refresh_rate", "fast_charging", "primary_camera_rear",
  "primary_camera_front", "rating", "battery_capacity",
  "has_5g", "has_nfc", "brand_name", "fast_charging_available"
)
missing_before <- phones |>
  summarise(across(all_of(missing_vars), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "before")
missing_after <- phones_recoded |>
  summarise(across(all_of(missing_vars), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "after_recode")
missing_tbl <- left_join(missing_before, missing_after, by = "variable")
```

**Which combinations of smartphone specifications are associated with higher prices?**

- **`r nrow(phones)` smartphone records**, `r ncol(phones)` original variables.
- Specifications, connectivity, brands, recorded ratings and prices support a business study of **pricing and competitive positioning**.
- PCA summarises related specifications. Linear regression relates the components and five additional predictors to log price.

Source: [Abdur Rahman, *Smartphone Models Dataset*, Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/abdurrahman22224/smartphone-new-data).

::: notes
One record is a listed smartphone model/variant, not a buyer. This is an observational dataset: describe associations, not causal effects. The CSV is a snapshot. Do not present its prices as current market prices. Collection date and sampling method have not been established.
:::

## PCA input variables {.smaller}

| Variable               | Type    | Meaning / unit                    |
|------------------------|---------|-----------------------------------|
| `processor_speed`      | Numeric | Processor speed (GHz)             |
| `ram_capacity`         | Numeric | RAM (GB)                          |
| `internal_memory`      | Numeric | Internal storage (GB)             |
| `refresh_rate`         | Numeric | Display refresh rate (Hz)         |
| `fast_charging`        | Numeric | Fast-charging power (W)           |
| `primary_camera_rear`  | Numeric | Main rear-camera resolution (MP)  |
| `primary_camera_front` | Numeric | Main front-camera resolution (MP) |

Inputs are standardised because their units differ. Charging power is zero when unavailable. Megapixels measure resolution, not overall image quality.

## Outcome and extra predictors {.smaller}

| Variable           | Type        | Meaning / role                 |
|--------------------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| `price`            | Numeric     | Recorded price (source units)  |
| `log_price`        | Numeric     | Natural log of price (outcome) |
| `rating`           | Numeric     | Recorded product rating        |
| `battery_capacity` | Numeric     | Battery capacity (mAh)         |
| `has_5g`           | Categorical | 5G available: FALSE / TRUE     |
| `has_nfc`          | Categorical | NFC available: FALSE / TRUE    |
| `brand_group`      | Categorical | Top five brands plus Other     |

The **five extra predictors** are rating, battery capacity, 5G, NFC and brand group: two numeric and three categorical.

::: notes
NFC means near-field communication. The source page could not establish the exact currency or rating methodology during this review. Verify these before final submission. Do not label rating as customer satisfaction or invent a currency. If rating is derived from specifications, acknowledge its overlap with the PCA inputs when interpreting the regression.
:::

## Preparation variables {.smaller}

| Variable                  | Type              | Meaning / use                 |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `brand_name`              | Categorical       | Original manufacturer         |
| `fast_charging_available` | Categorical (0/1) | Fast charging available (0/1) |
| `PC1` to `PC`*k*          | Numeric           | Weighted standardised specs   |

**Brand groups:** Oppo, Realme, Samsung, Vivo, Xiaomi and Other, selected by frequency in the original dataset. Other combines all remaining brands.

Price is excluded from PCA. The five additional predictors are also excluded from component construction.

::: notes
brand_name is used to derive brand_group. fast_charging_available distinguishes unavailable charging from unknown charging power. Each PC is a weighted combination of the seven standardised inputs. The number of PCs, k, follows the 70% cumulative-variance rule.
:::

## Why this dataset suits PCA

- **Business relevance:** manufacturers and retailers need to understand specification bundles and product positioning.
- **Correlated inputs:** RAM and storage correlate at **`r round(correlation_matrix["ram_capacity", "internal_memory"], 2)`** in the complete records, suggesting shared information.
- **Suitable structure:** seven numeric PCA inputs, a numeric outcome, and both numeric and categorical additional predictors.
- **Usable sample:** `r nrow(phones_clean)` complete records remain. The PCA uses `r nrow(phone_training)` training records.

## Objectives and significance {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Objectives**

1.  Summarise related smartphone specifications into components and interpret their specification profiles.
2.  Examine how the components and five additional predictors are associated with smartphone price.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Who benefits?**

- **Manufacturers:** compare specification bundles when positioning products.
- **Retailers:** compare models when planning price ranges and product assortments.
- **Buyers and analysts:** understand complex specifications through fewer dimensions.
:::

## Missing values and cleaning {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-missing
#| tbl-cap: "Missing values before and after recoding"
missing_tbl |>
  filter(before > 0) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(variable = "Variable", before = "Original NAs", after_recode = "After recoding")
```

All other used source variables have zero missing values. Of 211 missing fast-charging values, **143 mean unavailable** and become zero, while **68 remain unknown**.

Removing records incomplete on the selected analysis variables leaves **`r nrow(phones_clean)` of `r nrow(phones)` phones** (`r round(100 * (1 - nrow(phones_clean) / nrow(phones)), 1)`% excluded).

::: notes
The full missing-value table, including zero counts, is available as missing_tbl in the setup. Do not add missing counts to calculate dropped rows because a record can be missing more than one field. Remaining unknown fast-charging values are not recoded to zero. Excluding incomplete records can change the sample composition. Findings describe the retained records.
:::

## Descriptive summary: PCA inputs {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spec-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the seven PCA inputs"
numeric_summary |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pca_vars)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric), decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(variable = "Specification", mean = "Mean", sd = "SD", median = "Median", min = "Min", max = "Max")
```

Summary of **`r nrow(phones_clean)` complete records**, before splitting. Different units and ranges support standardising the inputs before PCA.

## Descriptive summary: outcome and other predictors {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-other-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of log price, rating and battery capacity"
numeric_summary |>
  filter(variable %in% c("log_price", "rating", "battery_capacity")) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric), decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(variable = "Variable", mean = "Mean", sd = "SD", median = "Median", min = "Min", max = "Max")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-connectivity
#| tbl-cap: "Connectivity features in the complete records"
phones_clean |>
  select(has_5g, has_nfc) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "feature", values_to = "available") |>
  count(feature, available) |>
  group_by(feature) |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = percent, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(feature = "Feature", available = "Available", n = "Phones", percent = "%")
```

## Why use log price?

```{r}
#| label: fig-price
#| fig-cap: "Price before and after the natural-log transformation"
#| fig-height: 3.5
phones |>
  transmute(price, log_price = log(price)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#2C7FB8", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Recorded value (price in source currency units)", y = "Number of phones") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15)
```

Across the **`r nrow(phones)` original records**, price has a long upper tail. Taking the natural log compresses this tail and lets the model describe proportional price differences.

::: notes
A skewed outcome does not by itself violate linear regression assumptions. We use log price as a useful scale for price associations, not as proof that model assumptions are satisfied. Scenario 6 asks for fitting and interpretation, not predictive performance evaluation.
:::

## Specification correlations

```{r}
#| label: fig-correlation
#| fig-cap: "Correlations among the seven PCA inputs"
#| fig-height: 4.3
correlation_matrix |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("variable_1") |>
  pivot_longer(-variable_1, names_to = "variable_2", values_to = "correlation") |>
  ggplot(aes(variable_1, variable_2, fill = correlation)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(correlation, 2)), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#92C5DE", limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

::: fragment
@fig-correlation shows that RAM and storage are strongly related (**r = `r round(correlation_matrix["ram_capacity", "internal_memory"], 2)`**). Shared variation across specifications supports summarising them with PCA.
:::

::: notes
Correlations use all complete records. PCA loadings and the later component comparisons use only the training records. A strong correlation is evidence of shared information, not evidence that one specification causes another.
:::

## Component scores by 5G availability {.smaller}

The **`r num_pcs` retained components** explain **`r round(retained_variance, 1)`%** of standardised specification variation in `r nrow(phone_training)` training phones.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pc-5g
#| tbl-cap: "Mean component scores by 5G availability"
pc_by_5g |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("PC"), decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(has_5g = "5G available", n = "Phones")
```

- **PC1:** 5G phones average **`r round(pc_by_5g$PC1[pc_by_5g$has_5g == "TRUE"], 2)`**, compared with **`r round(pc_by_5g$PC1[pc_by_5g$has_5g == "FALSE"], 2)`** without 5G. All seven loadings are positive. RAM, charging power and refresh rate are strongest. This suggests a higher overall specification profile for 5G phones.
- **PC2:** both group means are close to zero (`r round(pc_by_5g$PC2[pc_by_5g$has_5g == "TRUE"], 2)` and `r round(pc_by_5g$PC2[pc_by_5g$has_5g == "FALSE"], 2)`). There is little mean separation on this camera-resolution versus storage contrast.
- **PC3:** the mean is higher for 5G phones (`r round(pc_by_5g$PC3[pc_by_5g$has_5g == "TRUE"], 2)` versus `r round(pc_by_5g$PC3[pc_by_5g$has_5g == "FALSE"], 2)`), a shift towards the refresh-rate side of the contrast with front-camera resolution and storage.

::: notes
These are descriptive differences, not significance tests or adjusted price effects. Interpretation is based on the current loadings: PC1 RAM +0.428, charging +0.414 and refresh +0.393. PC2 rear camera +0.752, storage -0.363 and front camera +0.330. PC3 front camera -0.649, refresh +0.438 and storage -0.333. The score is a weighted combination. A higher score need not mean that every positively loading input is higher. Coordinate component labels with Person C. Recheck this prose if the seed, input variables or cleaning changes. Keep the original training labels aligned when attaching them to baked scores.
:::

## Mean component scores by brand {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pc-brand
#| tbl-cap: "Mean component scores by brand group"
pc_by_brand |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("PC"), decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(brand_group = "Brand group", n = "Phones")
```

- **PC1:** Among the five named brands, Xiaomi has the highest mean (`r round(pc_by_brand$PC1[pc_by_brand$brand_group == "xiaomi"], 2)`) and Samsung the lowest (`r round(pc_by_brand$PC1[pc_by_brand$brand_group == "samsung"], 2)`). These describe sampled specification profiles.
- **PC2:** Xiaomi's positive mean (`r round(pc_by_brand$PC2[pc_by_brand$brand_group == "xiaomi"], 2)`) leans towards camera resolution relative to storage.
- **PC3:** Vivo's negative mean (`r round(pc_by_brand$PC3[pc_by_brand$brand_group == "vivo"], 2)`) leans towards front-camera resolution and storage relative to refresh rate.

::: notes
All means are computed from the training records. Other has the highest PC1 mean overall but pools many manufacturers, so it is not a single competitor. Do not generalise a sample's mean to all products a brand makes. The comparisons do not adjust for price or other predictors.
:::

## Within-brand variation in PC1

```{r}
#| label: fig-pc-brand
#| fig-cap: "PC1 scores across the brand groups"
#| fig-height: 3.8
pc_scores |>
  ggplot(aes(brand_group, PC1, fill = brand_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Brand group", y = "PC1: overall specification profile") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

::: fragment
@fig-pc-brand shows overlapping brand distributions. Individual models vary substantially within a brand. **Other pools several brands.** Component comparisons describe product profiles. Regression examines their associations with price alongside the five additional predictors.
:::
